VeraGridEngine.Devices.Dynamic.static_parameter_mapping_unified module

Unified API-object parameter initialization mapping.

This module contains the static-device to problem-parameter assignment layer shared by EMT and RMS problem builders. The contract is intentionally narrow:

  • Entries in Block.api_obj_mapping map ParamPowerFlowReferenceType keys to variables declared by the same block. Block.parameters declares immutable values and Block.event_dict declares event-capable values. The mapping only selects the initial value source; it does not select the runtime role.

  • Only values that come from the static grid device, or from static network bases such as Sbase and fBase, are assigned here.

  • Neither Block.parameters nor Block.event_dict is written by this module. Resolved values are stored in the problem-side mapping consumed by both RMS and EMT assembly.

The unified mapper combines two strategies:

  • automatic direct mapping for schema-declared dyn_ref properties whose semantics are true direct static-to-problem assignments;

  • explicit device-family mapping for grid-base quantities, derived electrical quantities, matrix contracts and historical aliases whose meaning depends on the target dynamic model contract.

The problem parser should call assign_static_api_object_mapping_for_device for each device model root. The function recursively visits all blocks, and the dynamic model template chooses which static values it consumes by exposing only the desired enum keys in each owner block’s api_obj_mapping.

Resolve device-backed initial values for a complete block hierarchy.

Both RMS and EMT call this public entry point once for each device model. Recursion is kept here so every descendant is treated by the same owner-local mapping rules and wrappers never need to duplicate a child’s api_obj_mapping entries.

  • device – Static grid device associated with the dynamic model.

  • mdl – Root block of the RMS or EMT model hierarchy.

  • problem_mapping – Destination for resolved initial values.

  • logger – Optional driver logger used for mapping diagnostics.

Returns:

None.

Assign static switch parameters exposed by mdl.api_obj_mapping.

The EMT switch template uses a closed-state conductance parameter in its dynamic current equation. The static switch device exposes series resistance and reactance in p.u., therefore the EMT template must receive the real part of the corresponding series admittance so the reduced EMT branch remains consistent with the static device data.

Parameters:

  • switch – Switch device.

  • mdl – EMT block.

  • problem_mapping – Dictionary with static parameters and their values

  • logger – Optional logger.

Returns:

None.

VeraGridEngine.Devices.Dynamic.static_parameter_mapping_unified.build_device_direct_dyn_ref_keys(device: ALL_DEV_TYPES) → List[ParamPowerFlowReferenceType][source]

Build the ordered list of direct dynamic references for one device schema.

The automatic direct-assignment path prefers the canonical list published by MultiCircuit.get_devices_static_params_mapping(). Small unit tests may pass lightweight grid stand-ins without that method, so this helper rebuilds the same per-device information locally from the concrete inherited schema.

Parameters:

device – Static device instance.

Returns:

Ordered direct dynamic-reference list declared in the schema.

VeraGridEngine.Devices.Dynamic.static_parameter_mapping_unified.build_device_dyn_ref_property_lookup(device: ALL_DEV_TYPES) → Dict[ParamPowerFlowReferenceType, 'GCProp'][source]

Build the schema lookup of direct static-to-dynamic references.

The automatic assignment path must read the inherited editable schema of the concrete device because many direct mappings are declared in shared parent classes. The returned lookup is keyed by ParamPowerFlowReferenceType so the dynamic template contract can be matched directly against the static schema declaration that owns the corresponding property value.

Parameters:

device – Static device instance.

Returns:

parse_connections_dict(datalist: Dict[int, List[Any]]) → None[source]

Parse serialized connections and replay their runtime alias state.

The saved connection table stores the graph that links one incoming variable to one or more substituted variables through their stable non-mutable identities. Rebuilding only the graph is not sufficient for the runtime symbolic system, because fresh GUI-created models also apply UID/name aliasing immediately when the connection is created. The load path must therefore reconstruct the graph first and then replay the same alias propagation so reopened symbolic models behave like newly created ones.

Parameters:

datalist – List of dicts with block_uid -> list of connection dicts.

Returns:

None.

parse_diff_var_dict(data_list: List[Dict[str, Any]]) → None[source]

Parse persisted differential symbolic variables into the factory.

The loader must rebuild each differential variable using the exact symbolic metadata stored in the .veragrid payload. In particular, the power-flow reference has to be converted back to the VarPowerFlowReferenceType enum so downstream EMT connection logic can distinguish branch terminal references such as vf_A and vt_A from bus references such as v_A.

data_list – Serialized differential variable records.

None.
